newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's real rises 0.01 pct on lower mini-band.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's real rises 0.01 pct on lower mini-band.

text.p: Brazil's real edged up 0.01 percent to end at 1.0295 per dollar in the commercial foreign exchange market, after the Central Bank set a weaker mini-band for the currency at 1.0295 to 1.0345 per dollar, dealers said.
The Central Bank set the new trading level for the fluctuation of the real by buying dollars at 1.0295 real and selling at 1.0345 reais at a morning auction.
Preliminary figures for commercial and financial foreign exchange contracts showed a Monday surplus of around 75 million.
The Central Bank bought dollars at 1.0295 real per greenback to drain excess dollars from the market and maintain the new mini-band in late afternoon.
The previous mini-band, set on Nov 7, was between 1.0285 and 1.0335 reais to the dollar.
Traders said an extraordinary auction of Treasury notes indexed to the dollar, which raised 473.8 million reais, did not affect trading in the forex market.
In the interbank floating rate market, the real dropped 0.09 percent to end at 1.0350 to the dollar.
In the illegal parallel market, the real closed steady at 1.075 per greenback, traders said.
